title: Plan of a flat on a grid of 1.5 m squares (5 rows, 5 columns)
bodyMd: The table is the floor plan of a small flat drawn on a grid. Each cell is a square of floor measuring 1.5 m by 1.5 m, and names the room it belongs to. Row 1 is the north side of the flat and Column 1 the west side. The edge of the grid is the outside wall of the flat. Wherever two squares belonging to different rooms share a side, an internal wall runs along that side; squares of the same room have no wall between them. Wall thickness is ignored.

data.caption: Floor plan of a flat on a grid of 1.5 m by 1.5 m squares. Each cell names the room that square belongs to.

accessibilityText: A floor plan of a flat drawn as a grid of five rows, north to south, and five columns, west to east; each cell is a square of floor 1.5 metres on a side and names its room. Row 1: Living room in Columns 1 to 3, Kitchen in Columns 4 and 5. Row 2: the same, Living room in Columns 1 to 3 and Kitchen in Columns 4 and 5. Row 3: Hall in Columns 1 to 4, Bathroom in Column 5. Row 4: Bedroom in Columns 1 to 3, Hall in Column 4, Bathroom in Column 5. Row 5: Bedroom in Columns 1 to 3, Store in Columns 4 and 5. So the living room is a block of six squares in the north-west, the kitchen a block of four in the north-east, the hall an L shape of five squares running along Row 3 from the west edge to Column 4 and then one square south into Row 4, the bathroom two squares in Column 5 in Rows 3 and 4, the bedroom a block of six squares in the south-west, and the store two squares in the south-east. The edge of the grid is the outside wall, and an internal wall runs wherever squares of two different rooms share a side.

provenance.notes: Original invented plan. A script walked the four sides of every hall square and counted 11 sides shared with other rooms (bedroom 4, living room 3, bathroom 2, kitchen 1, store 1) and 1 side on the outside wall.
